title: World roundup: UN warns of famine risk in Africa, Ukraine offers Black Sea ceasefire, migrant deaths off Canary Islands
key_points: UN food agencies list 16 hunger hotspots, including Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Uganda and Chad.
Ukraine offers Russia a ceasefire at sea to protect grain exports and waits for Moscow's answer.
At least eight people are found dead on a migrant boat near Spain's Canary Islands.
The US says it disabled another ship trying to break its blockade of Iran; at least 13 soldiers are killed in Niger.
content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the last 24 hours, with a focus on news that matters to Africans and Kenyans abroad.

UN: hunger to get worse in 16 hotspots, many in Africa

Two UN agencies, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP), said on Friday that hunger will get much worse in 16 places over the next six months, from December to May. That is up from 13 places in June, Al Jazeera reported.

Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen face the most serious risk of famine. Chad, Uganda and parts of Southern Africa were added to the list. The agencies said war is the main cause of hunger in 12 of the 16 places. They also warned that the El Niño weather pattern is expected to become very strong.

According to the report, aid to the five worst-hit countries fell from $5.1 billion in 2022 to $2 billion in 2025.

What this means for Kenyans: three of Kenya's neighbours, Somalia, South Sudan and Uganda, are on the list, and El Niño can bring floods and crop losses to East Africa.

Ukraine offers a ceasefire at sea to protect grain

Ukraine has offered Russia a ceasefire in the Black Sea to protect ships carrying grain and other food. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced the offer on Friday at a food conference. "We are now awaiting a response from Russia," he said, as quoted by Al Jazeera.

Al Jazeera reported that Russia wants oil shipping included, while Ukraine says oil belongs in a wider energy deal. On the same day, Russian President Vladimir Putin attended a ceremony for a new nuclear-powered submarine. Moscow says it carries hypersonic missiles.

What this means for Kenyans: Ukraine is a major grain exporter, and safe shipping helps keep world wheat and food prices stable, including in Africa.

At least eight dead on migrant boat near Canary Islands

Spain's sea rescue service said eight to 10 bodies were found on a boat carrying about 100 people near El Hierro in the Canary Islands on Friday, Al Jazeera reported. Six people were flown to hospital in serious condition.

The Canary Islands leader, Fernando Clavijo, said the emergency begins on the shores of Senegal and Gambia, and asked Madrid and the European Union to act. A record 2,100 people reached the islands in a single day earlier this week. Spain holds a general election on Sunday, and migration is a major issue.

US disables another ship near Iran

The US military said its forces fired on a Palau-flagged cargo ship, the Pacific Archer, in the Gulf of Oman and disabled its engine as it tried to break the US blockade of Iran. US Central Command said the crew was not hurt. Al Jazeera said this is at least the 15th ship publicly reported disabled since the blockade began in April.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said one tanker hit a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. That claim has not been independently confirmed.

What this means for Kenyans: trouble in the Gulf shipping lanes can push up fuel prices, which affects transport and food costs at home.

At least 13 soldiers killed in Niger

Gunmen attacked a National Guard base in Sanam, in Niger's Tillabéri region near the border with Mali, early on Thursday. Niger's Defence Ministry said at least 13 soldiers were killed and 20 wounded, Al Jazeera reported. The ministry called it a terrorist attack. It was not clear who carried it out.
